steps.name: Franka
steps.text: All squads are fully prepared and ready to return to the landship at a moment's notice.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Where's Jessica? Still can't reach her?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Her communicator... is broken again.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Twice in one operation? That's too much of a coincidence. What is that girl up to?

spans.text: Twice in one operation? That's too much of a coincidence. What

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Jessica, you're finally back!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Don't worry about it. Laura's already packed your bags.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's not that... I...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm... here to say goodbye.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Goodbye?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Are you applying for temporary leave?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I guess?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: And your reason for doing so?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Personal reasons. There's some personal stuff I have to do, no matter what.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: And how long will you be gone?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't know. Maybe a week, maybe a year...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Did you hit your head? Do you really expect us to grant temporary leave for up to a year?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If that isn't an option, then... can I hand in my resignation?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You're quitting?!

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Ah, right. You said from the start that you're here to say goodbye. And goodbyes don't need an application.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I don't know what brought this on all of a sudden, but I need to remind you: If you leave the team, everything you've worked so hard for in Blacksteel will likely go up in smoke.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Whatever it is you need to do, are you willing to trade all of your efforts until now for it?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: These are the last explosives left in the mine. Let's go grab 'em.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I'll do the inspection. You go ahead and rest for now.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Um, Leone...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Are you sure about this...? About blowing up the furnace?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I know I shouldn't be saying this, but you were so reluctant when we talked about blowing up the energy tower...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: If we don't blow it up, how else are we gonna seal the secret passage and hide Helena's whereabouts?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: As for what I personally think... It ain't important. Don't matter no more.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Ain't a single thing left in Davistown that can be fixed up.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: But if we get that money, there's still hope for us, someday down the road. Out on the frontier. Right?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...There will be. For sure.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Heh. Hope. Hope... Who knew one last glimmer of hope would be so damn expensive?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: But for this last bit of hope, for this ticket not to reach the end of the line today... I have to accept that, even if it costs me my life.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: I have no idea what you're trying to accomplish, Jessica, but can you guarantee you won't regret it?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: When using the welding gun, pay attention to the angle between it and the weld. Holding it too high causes spattering, and makes it easy to get hurt.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: For a woman who runs a diner, you sure know way too many things.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Heh. I spent more than two decades traveling across grand ol' Columbia. I had a lot of choices.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...When you got dumped, did you ever think about going home?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Dumped?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Oh, I get it. Leone must've gotten the wrong idea.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Nah, I'm the one who dumped him. He ended up being a real by-the-books sorta fella... Didn't suit that gruff face of his one bit.

spans.text: Nah, I'm the one who dumped
. He ended up being a real by-the-books sorta fella... Didn't suit that gruff face of his one bit.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Back then, I was dead set on travelling across Columbia with him, but he thought I was too wild... Still, we supported each other across the barrens, and I ain't saying it was a bad life.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: But one night, he suddenly proposed to me. Said he couldn't stand all that wandering no more, and he wanted to settle down on some plate.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Going through the same motions in the same place, over and over again? I couldn't imagine a worse punishment.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So I turned him down, left him all my money and possessions, and told him I'd make a terrible wife. Then I mounted my burdenbeast and rode off into the sunset.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But... you still ended up in Davistown.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: In his letter, he said he'd finally fulfilled his old dream, and wanted me to drop by to visit.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So I came here, thinking the whole trip about how to turn him down in a way that'd let him keep his middle-aged dignity.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: But... you know the rest. I was too late. He'd already passed away.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And then you inherited his diner and stayed...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I didn't inherit it, I recaptured it. It'd been ransacked by a gang of thugs. Must've fought off at least fifteen of 'em.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That's how life is. Romantic stories ain't always have romantic reasons. More often than not, the journey is just the punchline.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: All these years... Have you ever had any regrets?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Regrets?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Like, for eloping, for breaking up, for not being able to see him one last time. Or for staying behind in Davistown... Stuff like that.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I feel bad about a lot of things, but I wouldn't say I regret 'em.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I've enjoyed the results of my choices, and accepted the costs. All with complete peace of mind.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I don't know.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You made such a huge decision without even thinking it through?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's not what I mean. I've given a lot of thought to your questions, and I've heard other people's answers too. In a sense, I even agree with them.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But I can't just regurgitate what they said and let them make my choices for me... Because in the end, their answers aren't mine.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't know if throwing away my past life is too steep a cost. I don't know if I'll regret this later, nor do I know what'll happen to me in the future.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But despite all that, I have to do this.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Nevertheless, I have to reject Jessica Brynley's request to be temporarily discharged from the team.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I see... Then I'll have to resign.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Jessica...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Liskarm... Captain?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Even the slickest, most experienced veterans who don't give two shits about their job wouldn't throw around the word 'resign' as casually as you do.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: But I also have to imagine that maybe what I'm seeing here is... a Jessica who's finally cast aside her fears and self-doubt. A Jessica who's truly found herself.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I still object to your decision, vehemently, but if you've made up your mind...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry. I really am...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Give it a break already.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: ...And stay safe out there.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Jessica...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry, Laura.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: To tell you the truth, I had an inkling this would happen when I couldn't contact you. But if you've already made up your mind, can I get one last hug? Think of it as a parting gift.
Before Jessica can answer, Laura has already taken a few steps forward and wrapped her arms tightly around her.
With her back to Liskarm and Franka, she also stuffs a tiny slip of paper into Jessica's pocket.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: (*whispers*) Wait until we're gone to read it.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: (*whispers*) Take care... Stay safe.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Anything else we need to do, Captain?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Then... let's get going.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woodrow, are you and Leone really going to be safe out there in the woods? After the heist, there will definitely be a bunch of people after you.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You really need to start thinking about your own future, instead of fretting over us geezers.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I haven't given it much thought. Maybe I'll have plenty of time to figure it out from a jail cell.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Not planning on staying a mercenary?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I just don't want to spend the rest of my life on a battlefield.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Jessica... Whether you decide to keep fighting or to put the battlefield behind you, I just hope you won't blame yourself for not finding an answer.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: What did you end up choosing?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: After the Revolutionary War, I stumbled around blindly for a long, long time. Until I finally decided to live a boring life, day by day.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Does that really count as an answer?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Just 'cause you're the only one who thinks so, doesn't mean it's wrong.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You're still young. Got a long road ahead of you.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Will I... find my answer?
As she looks at the now-abandoned safe house, Jessica feels a soreness coming from her nose.
She sniffles and gives it a rub, then opens up the slip of paper from before.
Following the instructions of a few numbers scribbled on the note, Jessica turns to an inconspicuous corner of the safe house where she finds a partition made from wooden boards.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Five, six, seven...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: The back of the eighth board is hollow...
The cavity behind the board is filled to the brim with equipment, all brought here by Jessica herself when she set out from Blacksteel's landship.
Sitting on top is another note in the same style of scribbles.
'I take it you have unfinished business in Davistown. This gear should come in handy.'
'Just forget about everything else and do it. I believe in the choice you made, so believe in yourself, too.'
At the bottom of the note is one last line.
'Goodbye, Jessica. Hopefully, we already parted ways on a high note.'

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sorry, I'm not late, am I? I needed some time to sort through my gear.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's fine. We still got five minutes.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Where'd you get all this stuff?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: A parting gift from a friend.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Then I'll have to give 'em a right-and-proper thank you if we ever meet again.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: One last run-down. After we go through the door, Helena and Leone are in charge of clearing any obstacles and grabbing the money. Jessica and I will be on crowd-control, then we catch up afterwards.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Once the deed is done, Helena takes the money with her through the secret passage, while the rest of us draw attention away from her. Any questions?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: If only there were more explosives... We oughta give that bank a little surprise.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Settle down. If the info we got from Sylvia is correct, we'll need to save most of them to breach the last door.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: The key to our success is speed. We don't have much time. The mercs on duty will be back in half an hour.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Even if we can get the job done in that time, the explosion will definitely attract Blacksteel's attention. However, most of the mercenaries are back on the landship tonight, and it'll take them time to arrive.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If it comes to that, just leave it to me. I'll buy you the time you need.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Time to go.

steps.name: Terrified Bank Employee
steps.text: Who the hell are you—!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Hands off the alarm.

steps.name: Terrified Bank Employee
steps.text: Aaaaaagh—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: This is a robbery.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: As long as y'all cooperate, nobody's getting hurt or dying tonight.

steps.name: Jittery Bank Employee
steps.text: No way... How is this happening—

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Shh... See, you're in the same boat as the other young lady over there. This is your one warning. We won't be so kind next time.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Now then, folks. Just don't panic, and follow our instructions.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Those are the conditions for your survival.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Seeing how there are no objections, why don't y'all mosey on over to the main lobby and squat down with your hands on your heads.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: We all know each other here. No funny business.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Now move it!

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: You'll need to pass through a total of four doors to get to the vault. The first is the door to the reception area, which needs a key, but any employee can get it.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The second is a passcode lock in the reception room. The code changes every day, but there are certain rules.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: From what I've gathered, today's code should be...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Perfect. The reception room key works.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Next up is the secret door... Behind the tapestry to the right of the entrance... Over here. Looks like Sylvia was right on the money.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Seven, nine, four, four, six, one... It worked? Well I'll be damned. That girl's got one good head on her shoulders.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What's next...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Inside the vault, there are two more doors. One's a security fence, the other is a vault door weighing dozens of tons.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The security fence can be broken through by force, but because it's connected to the security system, the only safe way through is via passcode.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The code is split into three parts, one for president, one for the manager, and another randomly generated by a cipher.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The cipher is located in a safe inside the reception room, and you'll have to force that one open.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: How'd it go? Didn't damage anything inside the safe, did you?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Mint condition.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Can't believe your skills haven't rusted after not using 'em in years.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: What's the matter? That was an invitation for you to start bragging. I mean, ain't nobody else in this town with your skillset.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Don't mind me. Just worried how Woodrow's doing...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...And that's number twenty-two. Now you're all tied up.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Next up is—

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: I never imagined these would be the circumstances we'd meet again in, Miss Brynley...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'd recommend worrying about your responsibilities first.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Also, I've heard this bank keeps a series of secret numbers, two of which are held by you and this gentlemen here. I hope you're both willing to cooperate.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Now take a walk with us. If you're not feeling cooperative, well, guess I'll have to shoot you.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Pick up the pace!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Good evening, you two.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: H-Helena?! Wh-What's the meaning of this?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You got nothing to fear, sir. I just wanted to ask you a few simple questions.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Will you tell us the passcode, or do we tie you to this door and blast you both to pieces? Your choice.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Friendly reminder: it is not a crime to reveal secrets under life-threatening duress.

spans.text: a crime to reveal secrets under life-threatening duress.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: You damn thugs—

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Five.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: Don't even think about it. You bastards don't deserve a single penny! You all deserve to rot out in the frontier!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Four.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: You complacent idiots put all your eggs into the mine, yet still have the gall to whine to the bank after getting wiped out!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Three.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: Nobody gives a damn about your rotten minerals. It's the era of high tech and automation now! Your only value to Columbia is to be thrown out to the frontier, the sooner the better!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Two.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: You filthy, uneducated hicks! You idiots don't even have a damn clue what numbers mean! Serves you right for getting tricked!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: One.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: Sixfivefourseveneightfour!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Hah... Never seen anyone spit out a string of numbers that fast.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Okay, now that your boss has squealed, it's your turn, ma'am.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Give me the passcode, or die.

steps.name: Bank President
steps.text: Hurry up and tell them already! Do you really want to die here?!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: ...Mr. Theremin, what would you even do with the money? Do you seriously think you can get rid of us and start over out on the frontier?

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Of course you can't. We're everywhere. We will follow your footsteps, and find you no matter where you go.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: The money you steal will smell as sweet as honey. And soon enough, our local associates will swarm all over you to eat it up.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: And with the promise of a few extra benefits, they'll even personally deliver your heads to us on a silver platter—

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: What's the goddamn passcode?!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: *cough*, *cough*...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Three... six... eight... six... five... four.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Go on, take it. You won't accomplish a thing, my friends.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Nothing will change. This tragedy is doomed to happen again and again—

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Shut up.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Shut up? It is human nature to be greedy, and Mr. Theremin here is a prime example. Had he not been so eager to cling onto things that never belonged to him—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You shut your mouth!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: How far you've fallen to mingle with this sorry lot, Miss Jessica Brynley.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Leone Theremin here could have left this place ages ago. Taken his children with him to Ironforge City, Nulaiteburgh, or Bunkerhill...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: What kind of blasting engineer wouldn't be able earn enough to put food on the table? How else would he have ended up like, if not for his greed?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Leone, she's right! The door's open!
Leone suddenly turns to look at Helena without saying a word. She is shocked to see the panic in his eyes.
It takes her a few moments to understand why.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Sorry, I meant... she gave us the right passcode.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: I know... It's fine. I know.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: If you manage to open the first three doors, congratulations. The last is merely an extra credit question. It appears the most complicated, but the solution is the simplest...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Blast it open.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Leone, how are the explosives?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Primed and ready.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Do it.
Like a precise surgical operation, the steel bars buried deep within the concrete are located with pinpoint accuracy and twisted until they break under the force of the explosion.
The fuel ignites under tremendous temperatures, bursting into layers upon layers of flames that gently wrap around the steel.
Then, at the moment it lets its guard down, all its defenses are stripped away.

The powerful backdraft caused by the explosion tears apart the stack of bank notes floating on the upper level, and the shredded paper is sent spiraling down the underground cavity. For a few moments, the snowfall here is heavier than it is outside.
The four people present are rendered speechless by this 'snow' that so many people could only dream of seeing.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Breathtaking...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Lord almighty, I've never seen this much money in my life.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: But it's also nothing compared to what the bank has bled from us.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: No time for idle thoughts, folks. Start filling those bags. We got more than enough to keep us busy.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Don't just stand there gawking... What are you thinking about?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Nothing in particular. It's just...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: This is the first time in my life I've ever wanted money so badly. It feels new... and exciting.
